input.quote: 10.5 Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed and construed and enforced in accordance with the laws of the State of New York applicable to contracts made and to be performed exclusively in that State without giving effect to the principles of conflict of laws.
input.rationale: Section 10.5 selects New York law, which matches our preferred governing law. However, the Agreement contains no dispute forum provision anywhere: searches for arbitration, jurisdiction, venue and courts return nothing, and the General Provisions article ends at Section 10.8 immediately before the signature block. The forum half of the rule therefore fails at both preferred and fallback level (no corresponding court designation at all), leaving venue open to any forum a party chooses. This is not walk-away territory (no foreign law or offshore arbitration), so we add only the shortest exclusive-forum sentence at the preferred level, with the customary temporary injunctive relief carve-out, and leave the existing New York choice-of-law wording untouched.

mappings.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.

proposal.summary: Add exclusive New York County forum to the existing New York governing law clause.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] New York law is already agreed, but the clause is silent on forum. We have added exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County, with a carve-out only for temporary injunctive relief, consistent with our preferred position.

ops.text: The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York shall have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits of any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement, and each Party irrevocably submits to such jurisdiction; provided that either Party may seek temporary injunctive relief in any other court of competent jurisdiction.
